summary: The article accurately explains the RBI's new rules regarding differential interest rates on bulk deposits and their indirect impact on retail FD rates, though it has an outdated figure for the bulk deposit threshold.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has allowed banks to offer differential interest rates on bulk deposits.
claims.note: The RBI has allowed banks to offer differential interest rates on bulk deposits based on their liquidity risk under the LCR framework.

claims.claim: This differentiation can be based on a bank's liquidity risk under the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) framework.
claims.note: Banks have the freedom to offer differential interest rates on bulk deposits by considering the differential run-off rate applicable to deposits or unsecured wholesale funding under the LCR framework.

claims.claim: While the rule directly impacts bulk deposits (₹2 crores and above), it could indirectly influence retail FD rates over time.
claims.note: The definition of bulk deposits was revised on June 7, 2024, to ₹3 crore and above for Scheduled Commercial Banks (excluding RRBs) and Small Finance Banks.

claims.claim: Bulk deposits are typically large sums, generally ₹2 crores and above, placed by individuals, corporates, or institutions.
claims.note: As of June 7, 2024, bulk deposits are defined as single Rupee term deposits of ₹3 crore and above for Scheduled Commercial Banks (excluding RRBs) and Small Finance Banks.

claims.claim: The RBI's framework for LCR is detailed on its official website.
claims.note: The Reserve Bank of India's official website (rbi.org.in) contains detailed information and master directions regarding the LCR framework.

claims.claim: The RBI's new rule directly applies to bulk deposits, its implications for retail fixed deposit rates are more indirect and nuanced.
claims.note: The RBI's new rule allows banks to offer differential interest rates on bulk deposits, and while it doesn't directly change retail FD rates, it can indirectly influence them.

claims.claim: Changes in the repo rate are a stronger indicator of future movements in retail FD rates.
claims.note: Changes in the RBI's repo rate directly impact the borrowing costs for banks, which in turn influences the interest rates they offer on fixed deposits.

article_title: RBI FD Rule Changes: Impact on Your Interest Rates
